title: Unconditional Unclonable Encryption
abstract: We give an unconditional construction of information-theoretically secure one-time private-key unclonable encryption scheme for one-bit messages, with efficient encryption and decryption and exponentially small unclonable-indistinguishability advantage.

bite.hook: Researchers built an unconditionally secure, unclonable quantum encryption scheme for one-bit messages.
tldr: They constructed an unconditionally secure, unclonable private-key encryption scheme for one-bit messages.
They used quantum mechanics to achieve information-theoretic security with efficient encryption and decryption.
They proved the scheme has an exponentially small unclonable-indistinguishability advantage.
bite.whyItMatters: Quantum mechanics allows creation of digital information that cannot be copied or eavesdropped on without detection. This proof shows unclonable encryption is mathematically guaranteed without relying on unproven computational assumptions.
bite.eli5: Imagine sending a secret message written on a magic bubble. If an eavesdropper tries to copy the bubble, it pops and destroys the copy attempt. This paper proves a way to make these uncopyable messages completely unbreakable.

glossary.shortDef: Encryption where ciphertext cannot be split into two working decryptable pieces.
glossary.eli5Def: A secret message encoded so that two people cannot copy and read it at the same time.

glossary.shortDef: Security guaranteed by mathematics and physics, independent of computing power.
glossary.eli5Def: A lock so secure that even a supercomputer with infinite time can never break it.

glossary.shortDef: A measure of an attacker's ability to distinguish between encrypted messages.
glossary.eli5Def: How much better an eavesdropper is at guessing a secret than just randomly flipping a coin.
